status_legend.designed: Specified in README/RELEASE_READINESS/STEAM_RELEASE/master spec but not necessarily coded.
status_legend.implemented: Source code exists that addresses the requirement.
status_legend.working: Automated test and/or a command run in this audit (npm test/build/lint/audit) demonstrates it functions.
status_legend.polished: Meets the master spec's own quality bar (visual scorecard PASS, QA test matrix, device capture) -- requires human/device review this audit could not perform.
status_legend.release_ready: Meets RELEASE_READINESS.md's ship criteria including production-host and real-device verification -- not achievable from a repo-only audit.

pillars.name: Core game loop (Boot -> Onboarding -> Hangar -> Map -> Briefing -> Flight -> Results -> Hangar)
evidence: src/App.tsx + src/ui/screens/*.tsx (all 10 screens present)
npm test passes (316 tests) but no test exercises the full screen transition graph end-to-end
unknowns: No automated or manual smoke test evidence was produced in this audit for 'no blocked screen' -- RELEASE_READINESS.md itself calls this a manual smoke test, not yet run/recorded here.

pillars.name: Flight physics (Rapier rigid body + custom aero model, gear, damage/detachment, fixed-step clock)
pillars.polished: unknown (no external playtest telemetry per README)
evidence: src/sim/{aero,flightController,flightModel,physics,engine,damageSystem}.ts
src/sim/flightTest.test.ts, aero.test.ts, engine.test.ts, damageSystem.test.ts, performance.test.ts, probe/*.test.ts all pass
src/core/fixedStepClock.ts + fixedStepClock.test.ts (per MERGE_STATUS 3.1)
unknowns: README explicitly states this is 'game-tuned rather than a real-flight trainer' and 'still needs external playtest telemetry before any public claim about difficulty balance or realism' -- treat that as an open item, not resolved by unit tests.

pillars.name: Aircraft parts/hardpoint assembly system
evidence: src/content/{parts,assembly}.ts + assembly.test.ts pass
unknowns: Only 'Frame Zero' (Tier 0) with two options per category is playable per README, against a spec that defines 8 frame generations (A0-A7, see spec section 24.1 asset register: PF_AIR_FRAME_YARDBIRD_A .. PROYECTONE_A). This is a scope gap between spec and shipped content, explicitly acknowledged by README, not a hidden defect.

pillars.name: 8-region streamed campaign world with weather/gust/vegetation/landmarks
evidence: src/content/regions.ts: 8 region ids confirmed by direct grep (the_field, scrap_valley, red_canyon, backcountry, coast_run, industrial_belt, high_desert_test_range, the_range)
src/world/*.ts (chunks, vegetation, landmarks, floatingOrigin, biomeWeights, terrainQuery, waterBodies, etc.) all have passing tests
src/render/worldVisualIdentity.ts assigns one landmark glyph per terrain family (data-driven, tested)
unknowns: VISUAL_STATE.md's own stated bottleneck: 'later-region prop density/material variety still need device-profiled capture review before an art-complete claim.' VIS-002/VIS-003/VIS-004 in VISUAL_DEBT.md are open/in-progress, not resolved.

pillars.name: 3D asset production pipeline (Blender source -> GLB export -> runtime streaming)
evidence: 361 GLB files exist on disk across airframes/upgrades/world/micro (see ASSET_PROVENANCE.json)

Only the 'world' domain (23 of 26 world glbs referenced) and a single hardcoded 'airframe' id ('hero_ultralight') are ever passed to assetLibrary.load() -- confirmed by exhaustive grep of every .load()/assetUrl() call site in src/
unknowns: 69 of 70 exported airframes (per-tier/-generation variants), all 19 'upgrade' models, and all 245 'micro' models (110 air_mic, 105 env_mic, 30 vfx) are exported and licensed as original art but have ZERO runtime call sites. This is 'designed + exported' but not 'implemented' in the sense of being reachable in the running game. Not previously called out in VISUAL_DEBT.md.

pillars.name: Cash/RP economy, tech tree, paint customization, home-base upgrades
evidence: src/content/{economy,techtree,reputation,homeBase,missionProgress}.ts all with passing *.test.ts
unknowns: README: 'a full inventory/workshop-upgrade loop is not' implemented -- explicit scope note, not a bug.

pillars.name: Keyboard path, focus visibility, text size, reduced motion, color-blind alternatives, WCAG 2.2 AA
evidence: aria-*/reduced-motion/focus-related code present in 12+ files including App.tsx, FlightHud.tsx, MenuNavigation.tsx, Screens.css, SettingsScreen.tsx (grep-confirmed)
unknowns: RELEASE_READINESS.md explicitly requires 'manual audit plus automated accessibility scan' targeting WCAG 2.2 AA. No Lighthouse/axe run was performed in this audit (requires a served build, out of scope for a repo-only pass). Presence of aria attributes is not proof of conformance.

unknowns: RELEASE_READINESS.md requires a 'mobile device test after deployment' over HTTPS. This audit only confirmed the build compiles; install/offline/update behavior on a real host is unverified.

pillars.name: Electron desktop shell for macOS/Windows/Linux + Steam release path
evidence: electron/main.cjs (untracked)
package.json desktop:* scripts + electron-builder config (uncommitted)

STEAM_RELEASE.md itself claims 'packaged macOS universal build has been smoke-tested locally' -- this audit did NOT re-run npm run desktop:package (out of scope: alters build/, long-running, not requested) so that claim is unverified by this pass
unknowns: This entire pillar is uncommitted working-tree state. If the working tree were lost, none of it exists in git history.

STEAM_RELEASE.md's own checklist lists Steamworks account creation, code signing/notarization, depot config, and store page as unstartable from the repo alone -- correctly scoped as out-of-repo work by the doc itself.
